subject: Clarify SKU aggregation, truncation billing and minimum unit rounding
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@orbitale.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Cc: procurements@orbitale.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Billing rules for long-context calls / how truncation is billed

Hi Dylan,

Hope you’re well — we’re finalizing the SOW and had a couple of quick but material questions from procurement on how Redwood bills long-context requests. Two scenarios came up and procurement needs clear, sketched examples for their finance team:

1) Long prompt + short reply where the model truncates the response because of safety/length — do you charge for the full generated token budget or only the tokens actually emitted? How does rounding/minimums apply?

2) Hybrid calls where we send a 50k token context (split into multiple chunks client-side) and then issue a short completion call that only uses the last chunk — does Redwood charge for the full ingested context (50k) or just the chunk used to condition the model?

Also they want to understand SKU aggregation: if we batch 15 requests in a single RPC to your API with shared context caching, is billing per RPC or per logical request?

We attached the draft SOW for reference (draft_SOW.pdf). Could you provide concise examples and any recommended contract language (rounding/minimums paragraphs) so procurement can proceed?

Thanks — Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Integrations, Orbitale Labs
agomez@orbitale.com

---

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Gomez <agomez@orbitale.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, procurements@orbitale.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing rules for long-context calls / how truncation is billed

Alicia — thanks for the clear asks and the SOW. Quick answers up front, then Kim & Naomi will add formal wording/examples:

- Truncation: you are billed for tokens actually processed (inputs + emitted outputs). If the model stops early due to safety or truncation, you are charged only for tokens emitted + the input tokens that were consumed. We do not bill for a pre-allocated "budget" that was not used.

- Large context / chunking: billing is based on the tokens the runtime had to materialize to evaluate the request. If you send 50k tokens but the runtime only loaded the final 4k chunk into the active KV cache that was needed to produce the completion, charges reflect the consumed working set plus any cached prefix that contributed to the computation. In practice that means you may be charged for more than the single chunk, but not always the entire 50k. Caching and prefix reuse reduce repeated charge.

- Batched RPCs: we bill at the logical request level (per logical call). If you batch 15 logical requests into a single transport RPC and they’re executed as 15 independent inferences, they are metered as 15 requests. If they can be collapsed into a single inference with shared KV prefix reuse and we can amortize the prefix, the billed work will reflect the merged computation.

I’m attaching the internal playbook link for a short read — Kim/Naomi, could you add a short worked example (numbers) and a suggested paragraph for the SOW about rounding/minimums? Alicia, I’ll also draft a one-paragraph contract blurb once we agree the math.

Thanks,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Alicia Gomez <agomez@orbitale.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, procurements@orbitale.com
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 08:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Billing rules for long-context calls / how truncation is billed

Thanks for looping me in — short worked examples below to make the rules tangible for procurement. I’ll keep the language snappy for copy/paste into SOWs.

Example A — truncation mid-generation
- Input tokens: 1,200
- Generation budget requested: 2,000 tokens
- Model emits: 480 tokens then stops (safety/truncation)
- Billed = 1,200 (input) + 480 (emitted output) = 1,680 tokens
- Rounding: we round billed tokens up to the nearest billing quantum (our standard quantum is 10 tokens). In this case billed = ceil(1,680 / 10) * 10 = 1,680 (no change).

Example B — large-context chunking (client-side chunked upload)
- You post 50,000 tokens split as 5 chunks (10k each) as part of a single logical conversation. The inference only needs the final chunk + recent KV prefix to produce the output; the runtime rehydrates 6k tokens from cache + the 4k from the last chunk into the active working set.
- Billed tokens = tokens loaded into working set (6,000) + 4,000 (last chunk keys used) + output (200) = 10,200 tokens
- Rounding to 10-token quantum => ceil(10,200 / 10) * 10 = 10,200

Notes on caching: if subsequent requests reuse the same prefix and are within the cache TTL, that prefix’s cost is amortized and your per-request bill drops.

Example C — batched RPC vs logical requests
- If you send 15 independent prompts in one transport RPC and they are executed separately, billed work = sum(billed tokens per logical prompt). If you merge them into a single structured input so the runtime can compute common prefixes once, billed work may be much lower.

Suggested SOW paragraph (copy/paste):
"Redwood bills actual tokens processed (input + emitted output). Billing units are rounded up to the standard billing quantum (10 tokens). Where context is provided in multiple chunks, charges reflect the tokens the inference engine needed to materialize and compute the result (including any prefix rehydration). Caching, prefix reuse, and batching behavior can reduce billed tokens; Redwood will provide sample invoice items on request to illustrate amortization for high-volume workflows."

Attachment: I added the same worked examples to the internal playbook PDF (redwood_billing_playbook.pdf) for procurement to review.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Product Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, procurements@orbitale.com

Subject: Re: Billing rules for long-context calls / how truncation is billed

Alicia — adding the commercial side and a suggested concession to help close the SOW.

- Recommendation: offer Orbitale a 10% committed-volume discount on token rates for the first 12 months in exchange for a 6-month minimum commit. This covers their finance team's need for predictable unit economics while preserving meter-level fairness (we still bill on tokens consumed).

- Contract clause to include (concise):
"Unit charges are computed on actual tokens processed (input + emitted output) and rounded up to the billing quantum (10 tokens). Committed discounts apply to billed tokens after rounding. Where token amortization applies (cached prefixes, shared computation), Redwood will provide illustrative invoice line items for the first two billing cycles to demonstrate realized amortization."

- Next steps: Dylan — can you put this concession into the deal record (DEAL-8843) and propose a redline for the SOW? Alicia — if procurement agrees to the 6-month commit + 10% discount, we can issue a clean SOW + procurement-ready clause.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
